planting.note: Pot divisions in a humus-rich, free-draining terrestrial orchid mix in full to deep shade; this historic cross is grown more for its place as the first-ever artificial orchid hybrid than for novelty, but it remains a vigorous, easy-blooming terrestrial orchid.

directions: Produced in 1854 by John Dominy, foreman orchid grower at the Veitch nursery in Chelsea, and first flowered in 1856, this cross of Calanthe furcata and C. masuca is recognized as the first artificial orchid hybrid ever raised to bloom, a milestone that opened the whole field of orchid breeding. Its flowers combine the hairy, forked nectar spur and deeply lobed lip inherited from the white-flowered furcata parent with the violet-lilac sepals and petals and deep purple lip of masuca, carried on an upright spike above a low clump of pleated, lance-shaped leaves. Like its parents it grows from small, sheathed pseudobulbs and flowers freely once established, making it an easy and historically important terrestrial orchid for a shaded bed or large pot. Divide congested clumps after flowering and keep the humus-rich mix evenly moist through the growing season, allowing a slightly drier rest once the leaves begin to decline.
